The translation of a SAS program as an R script

Source: R/script.R
sas_script.Rd

sas_script() turns the result of sas_translate() (the translation of the program, before it runs) or of sas_run() (the trace of that run: the code that ran) into a script: one call of a step verb per SAS step (sas_data_step(), sas_proc_sort(), sas_proc_means(), sas_proc_sql(), sas_proc(), sas_options(), sas_title(), sas_global(), sas_deferred()), each running its step in a session created by sas_session(). Printing the object writes the script; as.character() gives its lines.

Usage

sas_script(x, tidy = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A sasonr_translation (sas_translate()) or a sasonr_result (sas_run()).

tidy

FALSE (one session for the whole script) or TRUE (see Details).

Value

A sasonr_script: a list of step nodes, each with verb, lang (the call that runs the step), text (its R text), sas (the SAS text), sas_lines (its SAS lines), macro_stack (empty list), include (NULL), kind ("static", "deferred" or "traced") and comments (the SAS comments of the step: lines (the R comment lines), line, position ("leading" or "trailing") and place ("step": above the step verb, "body": above the line of the generated code of the statement, "after": below the last step)).

Details

Each DATA step is written as the R code sasonr generated for it, unchanged, inside sas_data_step(). A PROC SORT or PROC MEANS step shows only the options and statements the program gave; other PROC steps and PROC SQL keep their SAS text. In a translation, macro code whose result depends on values known only at run time (CALL SYMPUT, PROC SQL INTO:, %SYSFUNC, automatic macro variables) is kept as SAS text in sas_deferred(), which runs it through the macro processor; a trace has no such steps, but it is valid for the data of that run only.

SAS comments (/* ... */ and * ... ;) are kept as R comment lines: a comment on the line where a statement ends belongs to that statement, any other comment to the next statement. Comments of the first statement of a step go above the step verb; comments of a later statement of a DATA step go above the line of the generated code for that statement, or above the step when there is no such line. Macro comments (%* ... ;) and comments in macro definitions or in code a macro generates are not copied.

With tidy = TRUE the script has no session where it does not need one: DATA steps that run vectorised (levels L1 and L2) read and write R variables (adsl <- dm |> mutate(...)), and the script starts with library(dplyr) and library(tidylog) (tidylog then reports what each verb did; see sasonr_tidy_log()). The other steps (row loops, PUT or INFILE, macro variables, user formats, PROC steps, PROC SQL, global statements) run in a session block with a comment that says why; the data sets go into the session with sas_session_add() and come back with sas_work(s, trim = FALSE). The values are the same, but data sets made by the tidy steps carry no labels or formats into later session steps.

Examples

tr <- sas_translate("
data b;
  set a;
  y = x * 2;
run;
proc sort data=b; by descending y; run;
", work = list(a = data.frame(x = c(1, 3, 2))))
sas_script(tr)
#> # Translation of the SAS program, written by sasonr.
#> library(sasonr)
#> 
#> s <- sas_session(work = list(a = a))
#> 
#> s |> sas_data_step("b", \(work) {
#>   # ---- DATA B (SAS line 2) -- level L1
#>   # L1: no cross-row state
#>   .d <- sas_ds(work, "a") |> sas_note_read("a") |>
#>     dplyr::mutate(
#>       y = sas_arith(x, 2, "*", .at = c(4L, 9L))
#>     )
#>   work$b <- .d |>
#>     dplyr::select(x, y)
#> }, sas = r"(data b;
#>   set a;
#>   y = x * 2;
#> run;)", line = 2L)
#> 
#> s |> sas_proc_sort("data=b", by = "descending y", line = 6L)
sas_script(tr, tidy = TRUE)
#> # Translation of the SAS program, written by sasonr.
#> # Tidy form: steps that need a sasonr session run in a session block.
#> library(sasonr)
#> library(dplyr)
#> library(tidylog)
#> 
#> a <- sas_work(sas_session(work = list(a = a)), trim = FALSE)$a  # SAS character values
#> # data b;  (SAS line 2)
#> # ---- DATA B (SAS line 2) -- level L1
#> # L1: no cross-row state
#> b <- a |>
#>   mutate(
#>     y = sas_arith(x, 2, "*")
#>   ) |>
#>   select(x, y)
#> 
#> # In a sasonr session: PROC SORT runs in the session
#> .s <- sas_session(work = list(a = a, b = b))
#> .s |> sas_proc_sort("data=b", by = "descending y", line = 6L)
#> list2env(sas_work(.s, trim = FALSE), environment())
